q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of tomato ketchup per kg?
title: Tomato ketchup carbon footprint per kg
short: Weigh the tomato paste or fresh tomatoes, sugar, vinegar and spices per kg, and use supplier figures. Add cooking and pasteurising steam, filling electricity and the bottle or sachet, then divide plant energy by kg packed.

ul: Tomato paste by solids, or fresh tomatoes and the evaporation energy to concentrate them.
Homogenising and hot filling or pasteurising.

p: Report per kg packed. Concentrating fresh tomatoes takes far more steam than starting from paste.

example.title: Worked example: sauce plant per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 30,600 / 200,000 = 0.153 kg CO2 per kg
Add tomato paste, sugar and packaging for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
